outcome: The classification of possible configurations of connected components (ovals) of M-curves remains open in the same places it was in January 2024: essentially unresolved for degree 8 (Orevkov's 2002 classification of flexible M-curves up to isotopy is the best available, but the fully rigorous algebraic classification remains incomplete/near-complete rather than settled) and wide open for degree 9 and above, with no post-2024-01-26 source claiming to close either case.
summary: I researched what has happened since 26 January 2024 to the classification of the possible configurations of connected components of M-curves (the first part of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, restricted to the maximal-oval-number case as the bullet states it). I found no post-window result that changes this bullet. The only closely related recent arXiv work is 2606.21449, 'Hilbert's 16th problem for arrangements of curves on a surface' (submitted 19 June 2026), which generalizes the classical problem to arrangements of multiple curves on a surface (obtaining a complete classification for three lines plus a cubic and a partial one for three lines plus a quartic); this changes the question posed (arrangements of several curves, not the isotopy type of a single M-curve) rather than restricting it, so under §3.1 it is a related/variant problem, not a case of the stated bullet — I classify it as beside the question. It uses a custom Julia computational library (NWT) for managing large combinatorial databases and standard techniques (Bezout-type obstructions, Viro patchworking); no AI/ML system is used or mentioned. A 2026 Mathematical Notes paper by Orevkov and Puchkova on 'mutual arrangements of a plane real curve relative to an M-quartic with an oval-snake' is likewise a related configuration question (a curve's arrangement relative to a fixed M-quartic), not the general classification of M-curve configurations by degree, and again uses classical algebraic-geometric methods with no AI. I also checked a widely-circulated December 2024 press claim that a Brazilian team (UNESP) 'solved Hilbert's 16th problem'; on inspection (via the cited press article) their work addresses the second part of Hilbert's 16th problem (bounding limit cycles of polynomial vector fields via a new 'Geometric Bifurcation Theory'), a completely different bullet in the Wikipedia list, not the M-curve/oval-configuration question in this record, and used no AI or machine learning. No arXiv listing, Wikipedia update, or survey found any new resolved or partially-resolved case of the M-curve classification itself (e.g., no new settled cases for degree 8 or 9, no narrowing of the ~1227 a priori possible degree-9 schemes reported after January 2024). The Wikipedia article's own text is unchanged in substance from the frozen revision: degree 8 unsolved, degree 9 wide open.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2606.21449 arrangements-of-curves generalization or the Orevkov-Puchkova M-quartic-arrangement paper should count as 'partial' progress if one reads the Wikipedia bullet very broadly as 'anything about mutual configurations of real algebraic curves.' I don't think this is the better reading: the bullet as stated asks specifically about the isotopy classification of M-curves (single curves with the maximal oval count), and both papers pose a different question (arrangements of multiple named curves, or a curve relative to a fixed background M-quartic) rather than restricting the M-curve classification question itself. Settling either would not let a careful editor add a line to this bullet's entry.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement explicitly completing or substantially narrowing the list of realizable/prohibited isotopy types for M-curves of degree 8 (closing the 'almost complete' gap) or degree 9 (reducing the ~1227 a priori schemes), dated after 26 January 2024, would settle this as at least `partial`. I found no such source.
